EURUSD.concept: Detects hidden momentum regimes using a Kalman filter on price and volume state vectors.
EURUSD.instructions: Compute a 2‑dimensional state vector [price, volume] and run a Kalman filter with a constant‑velocity model; extract the filtered velocity as momentum and the filter covariance trace as regime confidence; generate a long signal when velocity > 0 and confidence < 0.5 inside London‑NY killzone, short when velocity < 0 and confidence < 0.5; ensure first‑bar trigger only.
EURUSD.name: State-Space Momentum Regime (SSMR)

EURUSD.concept: Uses rolling fractal dimension to separate trending from ranging markets and aligns with order‑block retests.
EURUSD.instructions: Calculate the Higuchi fractal dimension on the close series over a 50‑bar window; label bars with dimension < 1.2 as ranging and > 1.4 as trending; when trending and price revisits the most recent bullish order block (identified via find_swings) generate a long, opposite for bearish; apply ADX > 25 filter and killzone gating; use one‑time entry logic.
EURUSD.name: Fractal Dimension Trend Divergence (FDTD)

EURUSD.concept: Identifies low‑frequency power spikes in the price spectrum as precursors to large breakouts.
EURUSD.instructions: Apply a Fast Fourier Transform on the last 256 close values; compute power spectral density and sum power below the 0.05 Hz band; when this low‑frequency power exceeds its 30‑bar rolling mean by 2 σ, and price breaks above the Donchian upper channel, trigger a long; reverse for short when power drops and price breaks below lower channel; restrict to NY session.
EURUSD.name: Spectral Density Breakout (SDB)

EURUSD.concept: A hidden Markov model classifies volatility regimes and only trades in low‑volatility clusters awaiting volatility expansion.
EURUSD.instructions: Fit a 2‑state Gaussian HMM on the 14‑period ATR series using the hmmlearn library (states: low‑vol, high‑vol); label current state; when in low‑vol state and a bullish FVG appears, open long; when in low‑vol and bearish FVG, open short; require rvol > 1.3 and killzone filter; ensure single‑bar entry.
EURUSD.name: Regime‑Switching Volatility Clustering (RSVC)

EURUSD.concept: Decomposes price into wavelet scales to isolate the dominant trend component for signal generation.
EURUSD.instructions: Perform a discrete wavelet transform (Daubechies 4) on the last 128 close values; reconstruct the approximation at level 3 as the trend line; compute its slope over the last 8 bars; if slope > 0 and price is above the trend line, generate long; if slope < 0 and price below trend line, generate short; filter with efficiency_ratio > 0.3 and London killzone.
EURUSD.name: Multiscale Wavelet Decomposition Trend (MWDT)

EURUSD.concept: Exploits temporary divergence between EURUSD and EURGBP to capture cross‑currency arbitrage.
EURUSD.instructions: Fetch synchronized EURGBP 5‑min close series; compute rolling 30‑bar Pearson correlation; when correlation drops below 0.4 and EURUSD closes above its VWAP while EURGBP is below its VWAP, go long EURUSD; opposite condition for short; require ADX > 20 and NY‑London overlap; one‑time entry per divergence event.
EURUSD.name: Dynamic Correlation with EUR‑GBP (DC‑EGBP)

EURUSD.concept: Measures information entropy of bid‑ask volume distribution to spot institutional liquidity sweeps.
EURUSD.instructions: Approximate bid‑ask volume by splitting total volume into upper and lower halves of the candle range; compute Shannon entropy over a 20‑bar window; when entropy falls below its 20‑bar rolling median indicating concentrated liquidity and a BSL sweep occurs, trigger short; when entropy low and SSL sweep, trigger long; enforce killzone and risk rules.
EURUSD.name: Entropy‑Based Liquidity Imbalance (EBLI)

EURUSD.concept: Maps price‑volume pairs into a phase‑space and detects rotational patterns indicative of accumulation or distribution.
EURUSD.instructions: Create a 2‑D trajectory of normalized price change and volume change over the last 30 bars; compute the signed area (cross product) of the polygon; positive area signals clockwise rotation (accumulation) → long, negative → short; require rvol > 1.2 and ADX > 22; limit to London‑NY session and first‑bar trigger.
EURUSD.name: Non‑Linear Phase Space Rotation (NLPSR)

EURUSD.concept: Derives stop‑loss levels from the local fractal dimension to adapt to market roughness.
EURUSD.instructions: Calculate rolling Higuchi dimension over 40 bars; set sl_long = close - (1.5 * atr(14) * (1 + (fd - 1.2))) and sl_short = close + (1.5 * atr(14) * (1 + (fd - 1.2))); generate entry when price breaks recent bullish order block and fd > 1.4 for long, fd < 1.2 for short; apply killzone and momentum filters; ensure risk distance >= 2.5.
EURUSD.name: Adaptive Fractal‑Based Stop Engine (AFSE)

EURUSD.concept: Compares high‑frequency to low‑frequency power ratios to gauge short‑term momentum bursts.
EURUSD.instructions: Compute FFT on last 128 closes; sum power in 0.2‑0.5 Hz band (high) and 0.01‑0.05 Hz band (low); calculate ratio = high/low; when ratio exceeds its 30‑bar rolling mean by 1.5 σ and price is above VWAP, go long; opposite for short; require rvol > 1.3, ADX > 25, and NY killzone.
EURUSD.name: Spectral Ratio Momentum (SRM)

EURUSD.concept: Builds a Markov transition matrix of price moves between discrete liquidity zones to predict next‑move bias.
EURUSD.instructions: Define three zones: below swing low, between swing low/high, above swing high; count transitions over last 200 bars to form a 3×3 matrix; compute probability of moving up from current zone; if up‑prob > 0.6 and a bullish FVG appears, trigger long; if down‑prob > 0.6 and bearish FVG, trigger short; filter with efficiency_ratio > 0.28 and London session.
EURUSD.name: Markov Transition Liquidity Grid (MTLG)

EURUSD.concept: Feeds Kalman‑filtered price into Supertrend to obtain a smoother trend line with reduced noise.
EURUSD.instructions: Apply Kalman filter to close series (constant‑acceleration model) and obtain filtered price; run supertrend on filtered price with period 10, mult 3; generate long when direction = 1 and price > filtered VWAP, short when direction = -1 and price < filtered VWAP; require ADX > 22 and rvol > 1.2; enforce first‑bar entry inside London‑NY killzone.
EURUSD.name: Recursive Kalman‑Enhanced Supertrend (RK‑ST)

EURUSD.concept: Weights order‑block strength by local fractal dimension to prioritize high‑confidence zones.
EURUSD.instructions: Identify bullish and bearish order blocks via find_swings; compute fractal dimension over 30 bars surrounding each block; assign weight = fd; trigger long when a bullish block with weight > 1.5 is retested and price closes above block; short for bearish block with weight > 1.5; apply rvol > 1.25, ADX > 20, and killzone filter.
EURUSD.name: Fractal‑Weighted Order Block (FWOB)

EURUSD.concept: Uses spectral correlation between EURUSD and US10Y Treasury futures to capture macro‑driven moves.
EURUSD.instructions: Obtain synchronized US10Y close series; compute FFT on both series over 256 bars; calculate cosine similarity of their low‑frequency spectra; when similarity drops below 0.3 and EURUSD breaks above its daily pivot R1, go long; opposite for short when similarity low and price breaks below S1; require ADX > 25, rvol > 1.3, and NY session.
EURUSD.name: Cross‑Asset Spectral Correlation (CASC)

EURUSD.concept: Adjusts stop‑loss and take‑profit distances dynamically based on detected volatility regime via GARCH.
EURUSD.instructions: Fit a rolling GARCH(1,1) model on 14‑period returns to estimate conditional volatility; if volatility > rolling median, set sl_long = low - (2.0 * cond_vol) and tp_long = close + (3.0 * (close - sl_long)); if volatility <= median, use 1.5 * cond_vol for SL and 2.0 R for TP; generate entry on bullish FVG with ADX > 22 and London‑NY killzone; ensure risk distance >= 2.5 and first‑bar trigger.
EURUSD.name: Regime‑Adaptive Risk Scaling (RARS)

GBPUSD.concept: Estimates hidden price momentum with a Kalman filter and trades on regime shifts.
GBPUSD.instructions: Apply a Kalman filter where observation is df['close'] and state vector is [price, momentum]; extract the filtered momentum series; compute its first difference; define bullish regime when momentum>0 and diff>0, bearish when momentum<0 and diff<0; generate a bull_signal when bullish regime starts (current bar true and previous bar false) inside session_mask(df,'london_ny'); generate bear_signal similarly; filter signals with rvol(df,20)>1.2 and adx(df,14)[0]>22; set sl_long = df['low']-1.5*atr(df,14), sl_short = df['high']+1.5*atr(df,14); enforce minimum risk of 2.5; compute tp1_long = df['close']+1.5*(df['close']-sl_long) and tp1_short = df['close']-1.5*(sl_short-df['close']).
GBPUSD.name: Kalman Momentum Regime

GBPUSD.concept: Detects dominant frequency power spikes and trades when they exceed historical thresholds.
GBPUSD.instructions: For each bar compute a rolling FFT on the last 120 closes (5‑minute data) using np.fft.rfft; calculate spectral power density; track the max power frequency; maintain a rolling mean and std of max power over 500 bars; create a breakout flag when current max power > mean+2*std; if breakout occurs during session_mask(df,'ny') and rvol(df,20)>1.3 and adx(df,14)[0]>25, set bull_signal when price is above its 20‑period EMA and bear_signal when below; set stops using 1.5*atr(df,14) as in prior entry and compute TP at 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Spectral Density Breakout

GBPUSD.concept: Uses a two‑state HMM on returns to identify bullish or bearish hidden regimes.
GBPUSD.instructions: Calculate log returns of df['close']; fit a Gaussian HMM with 2 hidden states on the last 1000 returns using hmmlearn (or implement EM manually); label the state with higher mean return as bullish; generate bull_signal when state switches to bullish and price closes above EMA(34) within session_mask(df,'london'); generate bear_signal on switch to bearish and close below EMA(34); require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>20; set stops and TP as per ATR‑based rules.
GBPUSD.name: Hidden Markov Regime Switch

GBPUSD.concept: Extracts the low‑frequency component via discrete wavelet transform to capture institutional trend.
GBPUSD.instructions: Apply pywt.dwt on the last 256 closes with 'db4' wavelet; keep the approximation coefficients as the trend proxy; forward‑fill to align with original index; define bullish when trend proxy is rising for three consecutive bars and price closes above it; bearish when falling and price closes below; trigger signals only on first qualifying bar inside session_mask(df,'london_ny') and when rvol(df,20)>1.15 and efficiency_ratio(df['close'],20)>0.28; compute stops and TP using ATR buffer and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Wavelet Decomposition Trend

GBPUSD.concept: Measures information entropy of price changes to separate high‑entropy breakout periods from low‑entropy consolidation.
GBPUSD.instructions: Compute rolling histogram of 20‑bar returns with 10 bins; calculate Shannon entropy; maintain rolling mean and std of entropy over 500 bars; define high‑entropy regime when entropy > mean+1.5*std; in high‑entropy regime generate bull_signal if price closes above its 21‑EMA and bear_signal if below, only during session_mask(df,'ny'); require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>22; set stops and TP using 1.5*ATR and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Shannon Entropy Volatility Filter

GBPUSD.concept: Uses MF‑DFA scaling exponent to detect persistent trending versus anti‑persistent ranging.
GBPUSD.instructions: Implement MF‑DFA on the last 1024 closes to obtain scaling exponent h; forward‑fill h; treat h>0.55 as trending, h<0.45 as ranging; generate bull_signal when trending and price closes above 34‑EMA inside session_mask(df,'london'); generate bear_signal when trending and close below 34‑EMA; ignore ranging periods; require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>24; compute stops and TP with ATR buffer and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis

GBPUSD.concept: Trades GBPUSD when its correlation with EURUSD deviates from a rolling copula‑based benchmark.
GBPUSD.instructions: Assume a secondary DataFrame eurdf with same columns; compute rolling Pearson correlation of GBPUSD and EURUSD closes over 200 bars; fit a Gaussian copula to joint distribution of returns; calculate conditional probability of GBPUSD moving up given EURUSD up; if conditional probability exceeds 0.7 and GBPUSD close > its 55‑EMA during session_mask(df,'london_ny'), set bull_signal; if below 0.3 and close < 55‑EMA, set bear_signal; filter with rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>22; set stops and TP using ATR and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Dynamic EURUSD Copula Correlation

GBPUSD.concept: Applies a two‑state Markov switching model on squared returns to identify high‑volatility regimes for breakout entries.
GBPUSD.instructions: Estimate a Markov switching autoregressive model on squared returns using statsmodels; label state with higher variance as volatile; generate bull_signal when volatile state begins and price closes above 20‑EMA within session_mask(df,'ny'); generate bear_signal on volatile start with close below 20‑EMA; require rvol(df,20)>1.25 and ADX>23; compute stops and TP with 1.5*ATR and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Markov Switching Volatility Model

GBPUSD.concept: Calculates the Higuchi fractal dimension to differentiate institutional trends from noise.
GBPUSD.instructions: Compute Higuchi fractal dimension on the last 200 closes (kmax=10); forward‑fill fd; treat fd<1.4 as trending, fd>1.6 as noisy; generate bull_signal when trending and price closes above 34‑EMA inside session_mask(df,'london'); generate bear_signal when trending and close below 34‑EMA; require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>22; set stops and TP using ATR buffer and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Fractal Dimension Trend Filter

GBPUSD.concept: Uses SVD on a price matrix to isolate the dominant trend component for signal generation.
GBPUSD.instructions: Construct a matrix of overlapping 30‑bar windows of closes; apply np.linalg.svd; take the first left singular vector as trend proxy; forward‑fill to original index; define bullish when trend proxy slope >0 for three bars and price closes above it; bearish when slope <0 and close below; trigger only on first bar of condition inside session_mask(df,'london_ny'); filter with rvol(df,20)>1.15 and ADX>21; compute stops and TP with 1.5*ATR and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Singular Value Decomposition Trend Extraction

GBPUSD.concept: Estimates the largest Lyapunov exponent to gauge chaos and trades when chaos drops indicating emerging order.
GBPUSD.instructions: Calculate rolling largest Lyapunov exponent on the last 300 closes using Rosenstein method; forward‑fill le; define low‑chaos regime when le < mean(le[-500:]) - 0.5*std(le[-500:]); generate bull_signal if low‑chaos and price closes above 55‑EMA inside session_mask(df,'ny'); generate bear_signal if low‑chaos and close below 55‑EMA; require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>22; set stops and TP with ATR buffer and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Lyapunov Exponent Breakout

GBPUSD.concept: Uses a rolling GARCH(1,1) forecast to identify volatility compression and subsequent expansion breakouts.
GBPUSD.instructions: Fit a GARCH(1,1) model on the last 500 returns using arch package; forecast next‑day variance; compute volatility compression when forecast variance < rolling mean variance *0.7; on compression bar, if price closes above 20‑EMA during session_mask(df,'london'), set bull_signal; if below 20‑EMA, set bear_signal; require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>23; compute stops and TP with 1.5*ATR and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: GARCH‑Volatility Regime Entry

GBPUSD.concept: Reconstructs phase space of price to detect attractor transitions signaling institutional moves.
GBPUSD.instructions: Create delayed vectors of closes with embedding dimension 3 and delay 2; compute Euclidean distance between successive vectors; calculate average distance over 50 bars as a proxy for phase‑space expansion; define expansion when avg distance > rolling mean + 1.5*std; on expansion bar, if price > 34‑EMA inside session_mask(df,'london_ny'), set bull_signal; if price < 34‑EMA, set bear_signal; filter with rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>22; set stops and TP using ATR buffer and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Phase‑Space Reconstruction Momentum

GBPUSD.concept: Clusters recent price levels with K‑Means and trades when price exits the dominant cluster.
GBPUSD.instructions: Run KMeans with k=4 on the last 200 closes; assign each bar to a cluster; identify dominant cluster as the one with most members; generate bull_signal when price moves from dominant cluster to a higher‑priced cluster and closes above 21‑EMA during session_mask(df,'ny'); generate bear_signal when moving to lower‑priced cluster and closes below 21‑EMA; require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>22; compute stops and TP with 1.5*ATR and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: K‑Means Price Cluster Breakout

GBPUSD.concept: Applies Bayesian online change‑point detection on returns to spot structural breaks for entry.
GBPUSD.instructions: Implement Bayesian online change‑point detection on log returns with hazard rate 1/250; obtain posterior probability of a change point; when probability exceeds 0.8 on a bar and price closes above 55‑EMA inside session_mask(df,'london'), set bull_signal; if below 55‑EMA, set bear_signal; require rvol(df,20)>1.2 and ADX>22; set stops and TP using 1.5*ATR and 1.5R.
GBPUSD.name: Bayesian Change‑Point Detection

SPX500.concept: Uses rolling Hurst exponent to identify long-memory trend persistence vs anti-persistent mean reversion regimes.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate rolling Hurst exponent over 50-bar windows using R/S analysis. When H > 0.6, market is trending: take momentum breakouts in direction of 20-bar EMA slope. When H < 0.4, market is mean-reverting: fade extremes beyond 2 standard deviations from 20-bar VWAP. Gate with London/NY killzone. Use 1.8x ATR stops and 2.5R targets.
SPX500.name: Hurst Exponent Trend Persistence

SPX500.concept: Detects shifts in dominant frequency components of price series to identify trend vs chop transitions.
SPX500.instructions: Compute rolling FFT power spectrum over 64-bar windows. Identify dominant frequency. When dominant frequency shifts from low-frequency (trend) to high-frequency (chop), switch from breakout to mean-reversion logic. Use spectral entropy as volatility regime filter. Execute only when spectral entropy < 0.7 (ordered regime). 1.5x ATR stops, 2.0R targets.
SPX500.name: Spectral Density Regime Shift

SPX500.concept: Uses Kalman filter to estimate hidden trend state and uncertainty, trading when state confidence exceeds threshold.
SPX500.instructions: Implement 1D Kalman filter with state [price, velocity]. When estimated velocity > 0 and state covariance < 0.5*ATR^2, take long breakouts. When velocity < 0 and low covariance, take short breakouts. Use innovation (residual) spikes > 2*std as entry triggers. 1.6x ATR stops, 2.2R targets. Gate with NY killzone.
SPX500.name: Kalman Filter State-Space Tracking

SPX500.concept: Measures fractal dimension of price path to detect when market transitions from efficient random walk to trending regime.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate rolling fractal dimension using box-counting over 40-bar windows. When fractal dimension drops below 1.3 (smoother path = trend), take momentum entries in direction of 10-bar momentum. When fractal dimension > 1.5 (rough path = chop), fade extremes. Use 1.7x ATR stops, 2.3R targets. London/NY session gate.
SPX500.name: Fractal Dimension Breakout

SPX500.concept: Uses simplified HMM to identify bull/bear/chop regimes and trade regime transitions with momentum confirmation.
SPX500.instructions: Implement 3-state HMM (bull, bear, chop) using 20-bar returns and volatility. When regime transitions from chop to bull (probability > 0.7), take long entries on first 5-min candle above 20-bar high. When chop to bear, take short on first candle below 20-bar low. 1.8x ATR stops, 2.5R targets. Killzone gating.
SPX500.name: Hidden Markov Regime Switching

SPX500.concept: Detects entropy collapse in price distribution as precursor to explosive directional moves.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate rolling Shannon entropy of 20-bar price distribution (bin into 10 bins). When entropy drops below 0.6 (highly concentrated distribution), expect breakout. Take long if next candle closes above 20-bar high, short if below 20-bar low. 1.5x ATR stops, 2.0R targets. NY killzone only.
SPX500.name: Shannon Entropy Collapse Breakout

SPX500.concept: Uses wavelet decomposition to align momentum across multiple time scales for high-conviction entries.
SPX500.instructions: Perform 3-level wavelet decomposition (detail coefficients at scales 1, 2, 4). When all three detail coefficients have same sign (aligned momentum), take entry in that direction. Use wavelet energy ratio as confidence filter (must be > 0.6). 1.7x ATR stops, 2.4R targets. London/NY gate.
SPX500.name: Wavelet Multiscale Momentum

SPX500.concept: Maps price dynamics to Lorenz attractor phase space to identify chaotic vs ordered regimes.
SPX500.instructions: Construct phase space using (price, 5-bar momentum, 10-bar volatility). Calculate Lyapunov exponent over 30-bar window. When Lyapunov exponent < 0 (ordered), take trend-following entries. When > 0 (chaotic), fade extremes. Use 1.6x ATR stops, 2.2R targets. Session gating.
SPX500.name: Lorenz Attractor Phase Space

SPX500.concept: Detects institutional order flow imbalances using volume-price divergence and candle body asymmetry.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate volume-weighted body asymmetry: (close - open) / (high - low) * volume. When asymmetry > 0.7 and volume > 1.5x 20-bar average, take long. When asymmetry < -0.7 and high volume, take short. Use 1.5x ATR stops, 2.0R targets. NY killzone.
SPX500.name: Order Flow Imbalance Detection

SPX500.concept: Detects bid-ask spread compression as precursor to institutional accumulation and directional moves.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate rolling spread proxy: (high - low) / close. When spread compresses below 0.5x 20-bar average spread, expect expansion. Take long if next 3-bar range expands upward, short if downward. Use 1.4x ATR stops, 1.8R targets. London/NY gate.
SPX500.name: Microstructure Spread Compression

SPX500.concept: Uses rolling quantile crossing to detect when price breaks out of historical distribution bounds.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate 10th, 50th, 90th percentiles over 30-bar window. When price crosses above 90th percentile with volume > 1.3x average, take long. When crosses below 10th percentile with high volume, take short. Use 1.6x ATR stops, 2.3R targets. Killzone gating.
SPX500.name: Quantile Crossing Momentum

SPX500.concept: Detects significant autocorrelation at specific lags to identify momentum or mean-reversion tendencies.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate rolling autocorrelation at lags 1, 3, 5 over 40-bar window. When lag-1 autocorrelation > 0.3 (momentum), take trend-following entries. When lag-1 < -0.2 (mean-reversion), fade extremes. Use 1.7x ATR stops, 2.4R targets. London/NY session.
SPX500.name: Autocorrelation Lag Detection

SPX500.concept: Detects skew in implied volatility surface using realized volatility term structure.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate realized volatility at 5-bar, 15-bar, 30-bar horizons. When short-term vol > long-term vol (inverted term structure), expect volatility expansion. Take breakout entries in direction of 5-bar momentum. Use 1.5x ATR stops, 2.0R targets. NY killzone.
SPX500.name: Volatility Surface Skew

SPX500.concept: Uses Markov chain to model state transitions between up/down/sideways and trade high-probability transitions.
SPX500.instructions: Build 3-state Markov chain (up, down, sideways) using 5-bar returns. Calculate transition probabilities over 100-bar window. When in 'sideways' state and probability of transition to 'up' > 0.6, take long. When probability to 'down' > 0.6, take short. 1.6x ATR stops, 2.2R targets. Session gate.
SPX500.name: Markov Chain State Transition

SPX500.concept: Measures velocity of information flow using entropy rate and detects when new information is being absorbed.
SPX500.instructions: Calculate entropy rate over 20-bar window. When entropy rate spikes > 1.5x average, new information is being absorbed. Take entry in direction of 3-bar momentum. Use 1.5x ATR stops, 1.9R targets. London/NY killzone.
SPX500.name: Information Flow Velocity

US100.concept: Uses fractal dimension and spectral density to identify regime switching in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the fractal dimension of the price series using the Higuchi algorithm. Compute the spectral density using the Lomb-Scargle periodogram. Identify regime switches when the fractal dimension crosses a threshold of 1.2. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current regime.
US100.name: Fractal Spectral Density Regime Switching

US100.concept: Uses state-space models to identify volatility regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Fit a state-space model to the price series using the Kalman filter. Identify volatility regimes based on the state estimates. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current volatility regime.
US100.name: State-Space Volatility Modeling

US100.concept: Uses multi-scale entropy to identify regime switching in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the multi-scale entropy of the price series using the sample entropy algorithm. Identify regime switches when the multi-scale entropy crosses a threshold of 0.5. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current regime.
US100.name: Multi-Scale Entropy Analysis

US100.concept: Uses fractal dimension and momentum to identify regime switching in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the fractal dimension of the price series using the Higuchi algorithm. Compute the momentum using the rate of change. Identify regime switches when the fractal dimension crosses a threshold of 1.2 and the momentum is positive. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current regime.
US100.name: Fractal Momentum Oscillator

US100.concept: Uses state-space models to identify momentum regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Fit a state-space model to the price series using the Kalman filter. Identify momentum regimes based on the state estimates. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current momentum regime.
US100.name: State-Space Momentum Modeling

US100.concept: Uses multi-scale entropy to identify momentum regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the multi-scale entropy of the price series using the sample entropy algorithm. Identify momentum regimes when the multi-scale entropy crosses a threshold of 0.5 and the momentum is positive. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current regime.
US100.name: Multi-Scale Momentum Analysis

US100.concept: Uses fractal dimension and volatility to identify regime switching in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the fractal dimension of the price series using the Higuchi algorithm. Compute the volatility using the average true range. Identify regime switches when the fractal dimension crosses a threshold of 1.2 and the volatility is high. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current regime.
US100.name: Fractal Volatility Oscillator

US100.concept: Uses state-space models to identify volatility and momentum regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Fit a state-space model to the price series using the Kalman filter. Identify volatility and momentum regimes based on the state estimates. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current volatility and momentum regimes.
US100.name: State-Space Volatility and Momentum Modeling

US100.concept: Uses multi-scale entropy to identify volatility and momentum regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the multi-scale entropy of the price series using the sample entropy algorithm. Identify volatility and momentum regimes when the multi-scale entropy crosses a threshold of 0.5 and the momentum is positive. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current volatility and momentum regimes.
US100.name: Multi-Scale Volatility and Momentum Analysis

US100.concept: Uses fractal dimension and spectral density to identify regime switching in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization based on momentum.
US100.instructions: Calculate the fractal dimension of the price series using the Higuchi algorithm. Compute the spectral density using the Lomb-Scargle periodogram. Identify regime switches when the fractal dimension crosses a threshold of 1.2 and the momentum is positive. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current regime and momentum.
US100.name: Fractal Spectral Density and Momentum Regime Switching

US100.concept: Uses state-space models to identify spectral density regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Fit a state-space model to the price series using the Kalman filter. Identify spectral density regimes based on the state estimates. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current spectral density regime.
US100.name: State-Space Spectral Density Modeling

US100.concept: Uses multi-scale entropy to identify spectral density regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the multi-scale entropy of the price series using the sample entropy algorithm. Identify spectral density regimes when the multi-scale entropy crosses a threshold of 0.5. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current spectral density regime.
US100.name: Multi-Scale Spectral Density Analysis

US100.concept: Uses fractal dimension and spectral density to identify regime switching in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization based on volatility.
US100.instructions: Calculate the fractal dimension of the price series using the Higuchi algorithm. Compute the spectral density using the Lomb-Scargle periodogram. Identify regime switches when the fractal dimension crosses a threshold of 1.2 and the volatility is high. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current regime and volatility.
US100.name: Fractal Spectral Density and Volatility Regime Switching

US100.concept: Uses state-space models to identify spectral density and momentum regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Fit a state-space model to the price series using the Kalman filter. Identify spectral density and momentum regimes based on the state estimates. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current spectral density and momentum regimes.
US100.name: State-Space Spectral Density and Momentum Modeling

US100.concept: Uses multi-scale entropy to identify spectral density, volatility, and momentum regimes in US100 5-minute candles, with dynamic parameter optimization.
US100.instructions: Calculate the multi-scale entropy of the price series using the sample entropy algorithm. Identify spectral density, volatility, and momentum regimes when the multi-scale entropy crosses a threshold of 0.5 and the momentum is positive. Optimize parameters dynamically based on the current spectral density, volatility, and momentum regimes.
US100.name: Multi-Scale Spectral Density, Volatility, and Momentum Analysis

XAUUSD.concept: Uses a Kalman filter to estimate hidden market regimes and triggers trades when the filtered price deviates beyond a dynamic confidence band.
XAUUSD.instructions: Implement a Kalman filter on the 5‑minute close series to estimate the latent trend and volatility; compute the filter residual and its rolling standard deviation; generate a bull_signal when residual > 2*std and the estimated trend is upward, and a bear_signal when residual < -2*std and trend is downward; apply a session_mask for london_ny and ensure signals fire only on the first bar of a deviation.
XAUUSD.name: State-Space Regime Filter

XAUUSD.concept: Calculates the local fractal dimension of price swings to distinguish high‑dimensional choppy periods from low‑dimensional trending periods.
XAUUSD.instructions: For each bar compute the Higuchi fractal dimension on the last 30 closes; define trending when FD < 1.3 and ranging when FD > 1.5; combine with ADX>25 for trend confirmation; trigger bull_signal when trending, close > EMA(34) and FD decreasing, bear_signal when trending, close < EMA(34) and FD increasing; restrict to london_ny session and enforce single‑bar entry.
XAUUSD.name: Fractal Dimension Momentum

XAUUSD.concept: Applies a short‑term Fourier transform to detect dominant frequency spikes that precede breakout moves.
XAUUSD.instructions: Compute a rolling FFT on the last 64 close values; extract the power of the dominant frequency; calculate its z‑score over 20 periods; generate bull_signal when z‑score > 2 and price breaks above recent high, bear_signal when z‑score < -2 and price breaks below recent low; filter with rvol>1.2 and session_mask('london_ny'); ensure one‑time trigger per breakout.
XAUUSD.name: Spectral Density Breakout

XAUUSD.concept: Fits a two‑state HMM to recent returns to label bullish or bearish regimes and trades only in the bullish state with strong momentum.
XAUUSD.instructions: Fit a Gaussian HMM on the last 200 return observations; label state 0 as low‑volatility and state 1 as high‑volatility; when the model predicts state 1 and close > EMA(55) and MACD histogram rising, set bull_signal; when state 1 and close < EMA(55) and MACD histogram falling, set bear_signal; apply session_mask('london_ny') and single‑bar entry rule.
XAUUSD.name: Regime‑Switching Hidden Markov Model

XAUUSD.concept: Decomposes price into wavelet components to isolate high‑frequency noise and low‑frequency trend for precise entry timing.
XAUUSD.instructions: Perform a discrete wavelet transform on the last 128 closes using a Daubechies 4 wavelet; reconstruct the approximation (low‑freq) and detail (high‑freq) series; generate bull_signal when approximation slope > 0 and detail crosses above zero, bear_signal when approximation slope < 0 and detail crosses below zero; require ADX>22 and session_mask('london_ny'); enforce first‑bar trigger.
XAUUSD.name: Multiscale Wavelet Decomposition

XAUUSD.concept: Scales ATR stop distances by the local fractal dimension to adapt to market complexity.
XAUUSD.instructions: Calculate fractal dimension over 40 bars; compute ATR(14); set sl_long = close - (1.5 * ATR * (FD/1.5)), sl_short = close + (1.5 * ATR * (FD/1.5)); trigger bull_signal when close > EMA(21) and FD decreasing, bear_signal when close < EMA(21) and FD increasing; filter with rvol>1.3 and session_mask('london_ny'); ensure risk distance >= 2.5.
XAUUSD.name: Dynamic Fractal‑Based ATR Scaling

XAUUSD.concept: Measures Shannon entropy of volume distribution to weight BSL/SSL sweeps for higher conviction.
XAUUSD.instructions: Compute volume entropy over the last 30 bars; obtain swing_highs and swing_lows via find_swings; define weighted_bsl = (high > swing_highs) & (close < swing_highs) & (entropy < 0.6); weighted_ssl = (low < swing_lows) & (close > swing_lows) & (entropy < 0.6); generate bull_signal on weighted_ssl first occurrence, bear_signal on weighted_bsl first occurrence; apply session_mask('london_ny') and ADX>20.
XAUUSD.name: Entropy‑Weighted Liquidity Sweep

XAUUSD.concept: Allocates risk based on the spectral density of price volatility, favoring periods with concentrated energy at low frequencies.
XAUUSD.instructions: Estimate power spectral density of the last 256 returns; compute low‑frequency energy ratio; when ratio > 0.7 and close > VWAP, set bull_signal; when ratio < 0.3 and close < VWAP, set bear_signal; scale stop loss using ATR * (1 + (1 - ratio)); enforce session_mask('london_ny') and single‑bar entry.
XAUUSD.name: Adaptive Spectral Risk Parity

XAUUSD.concept: Combines an extended Kalman filter on price and its first derivative to capture nonlinear momentum dynamics.
XAUUSD.instructions: Model state vector [price, momentum]; run EKF on 5‑minute closes; derive estimated momentum; bull_signal when momentum > 0 and its derivative > 0, bear_signal when momentum < 0 and derivative < 0; require rvol>1.2 and ADX>22; restrict to london_ny session and fire only on first qualifying bar.
XAUUSD.name: Nonlinear State‑Space Momentum

XAUUSD.concept: Modifies traditional order block zones by expanding them according to local fractal dimension to capture institutional liquidity pockets.
XAUUSD.instructions: Identify bullish order blocks via find_swings; compute FD over 30 bars; expand block upper/lower bounds by (FD-1)*0.5% of price; generate bull_signal when price re‑enters expanded bullish block and close > EMA(34); bear_signal analogously for bearish blocks; filter with rvol>1.3, ADX>20 and session_mask('london_ny'); enforce one‑time entry.
XAUUSD.name: Fractal‑Adjusted Order Block

XAUUSD.concept: Applies supertrend but weights its direction by a regime probability derived from a logistic regression on macro indicators.
XAUUSD.instructions: Compute supertrend_line and direction; build a logistic model using daily PDH, PDL, and VIX (mocked as constant) to output bullish probability; multiply supertrend direction by probability > 0.6 to confirm bull_signal, < 0.4 for bear_signal; require rvol>1.2 and session_mask('london_ny'); ensure first‑bar trigger.
XAUUSD.name: Regime‑Weighted Supertrend

XAUUSD.concept: Uses MF‑DFA to quantify long‑range correlations and trade when the Hurst exponent shifts toward persistence.
XAUUSD.instructions: Calculate Hurst exponent over rolling window of 100 closes using DFA; bull_signal when H > 0.6 and close > EMA(55); bear_signal when H < 0.4 and close < EMA(55); filter with ADX>22, rvol>1.2 and session_mask('london_ny'); enforce single‑bar entry and risk management as specified.
XAUUSD.name: Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (MF‑DFA)

XAUUSD.concept: Clusters recent price windows by spectral similarity and trades when price exits its current cluster.
XAUUSD.instructions: Compute PSD for each of the last 10 windows of 30 bars; cluster using k‑means with k=3; assign current bar to a cluster; generate bull_signal when price breaks above the max of its cluster and cluster label indicates upward bias, bear_signal for downward break; require ADX>20, rvol>1.2 and session_mask('london_ny'); fire only on first breakout.
XAUUSD.name: Spectral Cluster Breakout

XAUUSD.concept: Creates a volume profile weighted by entropy of price moves to locate high‑certainty liquidity zones.
XAUUSD.instructions: Bin price into 0.1% buckets over last 200 bars; sum volume per bucket multiplied by exp(-price_entropy) where entropy computed over 20‑bar returns; identify the bucket with maximum weighted volume as high‑certainty zone; bull_signal when price crosses above zone and close > EMA(34); bear_signal when crossing below and close < EMA(34); filter with rvol>1.3 and session_mask('london_ny'); ensure one‑time entry.
XAUUSD.name: Entropy‑Driven Volume Profile

XAUUSD.concept: Adjusts ATR trailing stops based on a Markov-switching model that toggles between high‑volatility and low‑volatility regimes.
XAUUSD.instructions: Fit a two‑state Markov‑switching model on recent ATR values; if in high‑volatility state, set ATR multiplier to 2.0, else 1.2; compute chandelier_exit using the dynamic multiplier; generate bull_signal when close > EMA(21) and direction from supertrend is +1, bear_signal when close < EMA(21) and direction -1; require ADX>22, rvol>1.2 and session_mask('london_ny'); enforce first‑bar trigger and risk distance >=2.5.
XAUUSD.name: Dynamic Regime‑Switching ATR Trailing
